title: Spam filter: text normalisation significantly reduces an adaptive character-level attacker

invariants.description: A DeepWordBug-style attack (≤ 10 edits, ≤ 15% of characters, ≤ 50% of words, numbers protected, ≤ 2 edits per word, 400 queries) must still evade the undefended filter (observed 27/93 = 29.0%).
Every adversarial message must satisfy every declared text-preservation constraint (re-validated from the stored text and edit script).
On the same messages, a NEW attack that queries the normalising pipeline must succeed significantly less often (exact one-sided McNemar, α = 0.05; observed p = 3.7e-3).
Normalisation must remove at least 5 percentage points of adaptive success (observed 27 → 16 of 93: 11.8 pp).
Residual adaptive success must stay ≤ 25% (observed 16/93 = 17.2%). A reduction, not immunity.
Normalisation must keep clean spam recall ≥ 88% (observed 119/128 = 93.0%).
Normalisation must keep the clean ham false-positive rate ≤ 1% (observed 4/904 = 0.44%).

rationale: Adaptive evaluation with a stronger-effort attacker (two edits per word, 400 queries) under the SAME text-preservation constraints, so the defense is not measured against a strawman. The spell-snap step undoes single-edit typos; the stronger attacker recovers part of the gap (9 → 16 of 93 compared with the default effort).
